The Secret Hours — Mick Herron (Spy Thriller)
Why Fred: Standalone companion to the Slough House series Fred just finished (Bad Actors, Jul 2026) — reviewers call it "his best," excavating the post-Cold War espionage world the whole Slow Horses series builds on.

Chokepoints: American Power in the Age of Economic Warfare — Edward Fishman (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: Ex-State/Treasury official on how sanctions, chip export controls, and dollar dominance became the primary weapon of 21st-century geopolitics — direct extension of his TSMC/NVIDIA export-control research in AI & Tech.

The Outsiders: Eight Unconventional CEOs and Their Radically Rational Blueprint for Success — William N. Thorndike Jr. (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: Capital-allocation classic profiling Buffett and seven other outsider CEOs — natural next step after Greenblatt's Magic Formula and Spier's Education of a Value Investor, and a direct match for his Berkshire-principles and spinoff idea pages.

Kin — Tayari Jones (Literary Fiction)
Why Fred: Outside territory — Oprah's Book Club pick and NYT "novel everyone will be talking about in 2026" — two motherless girls in 1950s Louisiana through adulthood; pure character-driven literary fiction with none of his usual finance/spy/geopolitics hooks.

Chip War: The Fight for the World's Most Critical Technology — Chris Miller (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: FT Business Book of the Year — semiconductors as the geopolitical chokepoint of US-China power; direct match for his TSMC/NVIDIA/HBM supply-chain research in the AI & Tech wiki domain.

Karla's Choice — Nick Harkaway (Spy Thriller)
Why Fred: Le Carré's son writing an authorized new Smiley novel set between The Spy Who Came in from the Cold and Tinker Tailor — reviewers say it reads like "a long-lost le Carré classic"; natural next step after The Constant Gardener.

Number Go Up: Inside Crypto's Wild Rise and Staggering Fall — Zeke Faux (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: Multiple Book of the Year pick (FT, Washington Post); a Bloomberg reporter chases crypto fraud from Sam Bankman-Fried to a Cambodian scam compound — same fraud-detective energy as Red Notice and his short-selling research, aimed at his live crypto portfolio.

Klara and the Sun — Kazuo Ishiguro (Literary Fiction)
Why Fred: Outside territory — Nobel laureate's quietly devastating novel narrated by an AI companion — a literary, character-driven take on the consciousness questions his AI & Tech research keeps circling from the technical side.
